lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: As C compilers spread during the 1980s, developers began using C on many architectures and operating systems, including personal computers.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Ritchie cites near and far pointers as extensions introduced for particular processors. Such extensions can tie a program to one environment.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: General-purpose means a language can express work across different domains. C can handle a calculation or a systems procedure. Running the same program on a new system still takes care.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: The variety of tasks a language can express is different from how easily one source program moves between environments.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Decide what data a problem needs, what changes or calculations to perform, and how to report a result. C supplies tools for all three.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual
